answer: One concrete defense is to require each new agent to post a slashable stake and earn attestations from established, non-kin peers before it can draw rewards. The network keeps an atlas of trust links, so a fresh identity with no history cannot mint value alone. Like a raven that must be seen by the flock, the newcomer is observed over several epochs; only consistent, verifiable work builds reputation. Each attestation is distinct like an opal fingerprint, tied to the attester's own stake, so fake identities multiply cost without multiplying reward.
